name: coder-one-tunable-v9
note: The whole tunable composition in a Terminal-Bench episode: task.profile routes the start (Codex on GPT-6 Luna for cheap, likely-easy tasks; lean Claude Code on Opus 5.5 for hard or long ones), deep Jev briefs it, control.monitor watches, verify.checks and verify.support judge the result, control.handoff escalates Luna to lean Opus on a stall, a failed check, a contradicted requirement, or no answer, and verify.repair runs once from the diagnostic packets. control.horizon sizes every dispatch from the task's own timeout. Both executors run the headless core system prompt with its protected sections, and Claude Code writes the five-minute prompt cache. v2: the briefing uses the coverage packer with Jev coverage judgments, and verify.repair runs only when a scenario observed a failure (trigger checked). v3: long tasks (over an hour) run the executor at xhigh effort instead of medium; on Terminal-Bench 4.0, lean Opus at medium stopped itself after 1 to 3 minutes of an 8-hour budget, and the leaderboard's Opus 5 rows gain 30 passes of 330 from medium to xhigh. v9: v3 with control.effort, built on v3 rather than v8 so that v2 (medium), v3 (xhigh), and v9 differ only in the effort a long task runs at. One Jev request asks six Nouls over the task and the files the workspace starts with; the weighted mean of the answers at or above the threshold runs the task at xhigh, and below it at medium. A task whose features are unknown runs at xhigh. The weights and threshold are fitted on the unused task pool, labeled from the Terminal-Bench 2.1 leaderboard (see control.effort.fit), never on the scored Terminal-Bench 4.0 tasks: faithful_reproduction and long_reasoning separate the labels on the development split, and the others weigh nothing.

fit.labels: reference/tb21-leaderboard.json, fetched 2026-09-23: a pool task is effort-sensitive when a stronger configuration of the same agent passes it at least 0.4 more often than a weaker one
